summary: Implemented the code-side id/FTS namespace bridge for the literature extension (8 of 10 phases COMPLETED): literature-doc-key.sh as the single sourced path-to-FTS-key anchor; literature-search.sh's get_project_doc_ids() rewired to union the path-derived key with .id, fixing project-filtered search for the 32 documents whose curated .id differs from their FTS doc_id; literature-briefing.sh's three .id-only lookup sites plus metadata extraction now tolerate .id // .doc_id; literature-ingest.sh rewritten to place new documents under sources/<id>/ and write a canonical parent entry (id == chunks_data.doc_id, never renamed) plus 1:1 child entries per chunk, with real title/authors/year threaded from Zotero (honest metadata_status='unresolved' marker, never fabricated, when no Zotero match exists); skill-literature/SKILL.md's /literature --validate no longer misreports a path-less entry as 'null (missing)' and now runs a WARN-mode namespace-divergence check; test-lit-pipeline.sh gained 4 new regression cases, each independently demonstrated red-then-green against a reverted fix; the domain doc documents the never-rename invariant and a completed 12-row reader survey. Every id-touching phase carried execution-based verification (byte-identical --toc output, real project-filtered search results, live-corpus divergence counts) per the plan's mandate that code reading is not acceptable evidence. Phase 8 (destructive/judgment-heavy data reconciliation in the user's real, separate ~/Projects/Literature/ corpus -- adding parent entries, adjudicating two duplicate chunk directories, resolving gabbay_2000) was marked BLOCKED: its own clean-tree precondition already fails (13 uncommitted lines left by a separate, unrelated, already-completed task never committed in that repo), and the duplicate-directory adjudication requires real content judgment on citation-grade personal data with no loud-failure safety net, unlike every other phase in this plan. Phase 10 was marked PARTIAL: its documentation tasks (FTS-namespace invariant, reader survey, fidelity-audit header note) are complete, but the --validate WARN-to-FAIL escalation was deferred since the live corpus does not yet conform (gabbay_2000 still has 0 FTS chunks) pending Phase 8 -- escalating now would make --validate fail against the live corpus immediately, which the plan's own rollback guidance treats as evidence Phase 8 is unfinished, not license to soften the check. Full reasoning for both deferrals is recorded in the plan's Phase 8 '#### Block Reason' subsection and Phase 10's deviation note.

artifacts.summary: Implementation summary covering all 10 phases: 8 COMPLETED with execution-based verification, Phase 8 BLOCKED, Phase 10 PARTIAL.
Phase 1 execution baseline: corpus counts, 5-document --toc probe set, divergence enumeration, confirms the pre-existing dirty state in ~/Projects/Literature/ is unrelated to this task.

blockers.description: Corpus data reconciliation in ~/Projects/Literature/ (separate real personal repo): its own clean-tree precondition already fails (13 uncommitted lines left over from a separate, unrelated, already-completed task, never committed there), and the required duplicate-chunk-directory adjudication (proofs_and_types vs girard_1989; van_doorn_2015_propositional_calculus_coq vs van_doorn_2015) requires real content judgment on citation-grade personal corpus data with no loud-failure safety net. Recommended follow-up: a human reviews and commits (or discards) the leftover task's changes first, then a future dispatch (or the user directly) performs the 15-parent-entry addition (low risk, mirrors validated corpus commit e6ce8bd9), reviews the duplicate pairs by hand, and decides gabbay_2000.

The --validate WARN-to-FAIL escalation depends on Phase 8's corpus reconciliation, which did not run. Escalating now would fail --validate against the live corpus immediately (index-only bucket = 1, gabbay_2000, confirmed by execution). Deferred until Phase 8 completes.
